privacy.title: Privacy policy | geoservices.space
privacy.description: What data geoservices.space collects, what it is used for, who it is shared with, and how to ask for it to be deleted.

how: Search by Browser: your browser asks you for permission and uses the location your device gives it (GPS, Wi-Fi or mobile network, depending on the device) to locate you. The coordinates are sent to OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) to determine which country you are in.
Search by IP: an approximate location is obtained from your IP address, which is sent to a geolocation service (GeoJS), without asking for permissions.
In both cases the map shows an approximate point, because a random variation of a few kilometers is added. The cell tower markers are illustrative and do not represent real towers.

To keep viewing the map, you are asked for a one-time payment that Stripe processes. The payment does not create an account or save your access: another search, or reloading the page, may ask for another payment. The price may vary depending on your country and is confirmed on the payment screen before you pay.
howSim: You enter a phone number. The simulator does not search for it or look it up on any network or carrier.
You see an animation lasting about 15 seconds and then a map with an illustrative point, chosen at random near the approximate location of your connection.

To keep viewing the map, you are asked for a one-time payment that Stripe processes. The payment does not create an account or save your access: another search, or reloading the page, may ask for another payment. The price may vary depending on your country and is confirmed on the payment screen before you pay.

faq.a: With the IP address, it usually gets the country right and sometimes the city; it can fail with a VPN, a proxy or mobile data. With the browser’s location the result is closer to your real position. In both cases the map adds a random variation of a few kilometers, so it is an approximate location and not an exact address.

faq.q: Can I locate another person’s phone?
faq.a: No. This site cannot locate other people’s phones and does not query any network or carrier. It only shows an approximate location of your own device.

faq.q: Why does it ask me for location permission?
faq.a: Only if you choose Search by Browser, so that it can use your device’s location. You can decline and use Search by IP, which does not ask for permissions.

We record your visit activity (for example, which button you used), your country and language, an approximate location when you perform a search, a browser analytics identifier, the campaign parameters if you arrive from an ad and, if you use the simulator, the phone number you enter. Your IP address remains in the server’s access logs, and the server uses it to estimate your country; it is only sent to a geolocation service (GeoJS) if you choose Search by IP or use the simulator. In the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom and Switzerland, measurement is only activated if you accept it in the cookie notice.

info.faqSimAnswer: No. The phone number mode is an entertainment simulator: it does not search for the number or query any network or carrier, and the result does not depend on the number you enter. It only shows a random point near the approximate location of your connection (or near Mexico City if it cannot be detected).

consent.title: Your privacy and cookies
consent.intro: We use cookies and similar technologies to measure how the site is used and how well our ads work, but only if you allow it. With your permission, Google receives data about your visit to measure site usage and, if you accept advertising, to personalize ads.

necessary.title: Necessary
necessary.text: They remember your language and your cookie choice, and the position of the map while you are paying. They are essential for the site to work and cannot be turned off.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.text: Google Analytics and the site’s activity log: which pages and buttons are used, along with your country, your language, your time zone and an approximate location, the Google Analytics identifier and the numbers you type in the simulator. They are used to measure usage and improve the site, and let your device remember your recent searches.

advertising.title: Advertising
advertising.text: Google Ads: they measure whether you arrived from an ad and whether you ended up buying, to evaluate our campaigns. Google may use that data to personalize ads and create its own cookies.

sections.title: Who we are
paragraphs: geoservices.space is a website that shows the approximate location of the visitor’s device on a map and includes an entertainment simulator. This policy explains what data is processed when you use it. The contact details of whoever is responsible for the site are at the bottom of this page.

sections.title: What data we collect
paragraphs: We collect this data to make the site work, to measure its use and to measure advertising campaigns:
items: Visit activity: events such as opening, reloading or closing the page, searching for a number in the simulator, viewing or zooming in on the map, opening the payment window, pressing the Buy button or abandoning the payment, together with the type of search you used (browser, IP or simulator), their date and time (and your time zone), your language and your country. In the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom and Switzerland, it is only recorded if you allow it in the cookie notice.

Approximate location: only when you perform a search. If you choose Search by IP (or use the simulator, which needs a starting point), your browser sends your IP address to a geolocation service to estimate an approximate location. If you choose Search by Browser and give permission, your device’s location coordinates are used. In all cases the map and our records use a position with a random variation of a few kilometers.

Phone number: if you use the simulator, the number you enter is stored together with the visit activity and, for as long as your browser keeps it, also together with that of your subsequent visits. For this reason, do not enter other people’s numbers.

Analytics and advertising identifiers: the Google Analytics client identifier and, if you arrive from an ad, the campaign parameters (UTM, gclid or fbclid). In the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom and Switzerland, they are only used if you allow them in the cookie notice, and the click identifiers (gclid, fbclid) only with the advertising permission.

Payments: Stripe collects the payment details directly (also your email address, which we see in the Stripe dashboard), and we do not see or store your full card number. We store the amount and currency of the purchase, and we associate the browser analytics identifier with the payment. The amount, the currency and a transaction identifier are also sent to Google to measure conversions, both from your browser and from the service that receives Stripe notifications.

IP address: our server records it in its access logs, as happens on any website. In addition, when the page opens, the server uses it to estimate your country with a local database, without sending it to any third party; that country decides the price shown to you and, if you have not chosen another one, the initial language. The application does not record your IP in its own technical logs.

sections.title: What we use the data for
paragraphs: To show the map, to choose your language and the price based on your country, to process payments, to measure and improve the service, and to measure the effectiveness of advertising campaigns.

sections.title: Who we share the data with
paragraphs: To provide the service we use providers that receive part of this data and may process it outside your country (for example, in the United States). The services your browser connects to also receive your IP address and technical data from your browser:
items: Google (Tag Manager, Analytics and Ads): measurement of usage and campaigns, including the amount and currency of purchases, and ad personalization if you accept advertising. Google also receives, on its own, technical data from your browser and the addresses of the pages you visit. In the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom and Switzerland, it is only loaded with your permission. You can see how Google uses the data at business.safety.google/privacy.
OpenStreetMap: loads the maps and, if you use Search by Browser, receives your exact coordinates to determine the country (Nominatim service).

GeoJS: receives your IP address, from your browser, only when you choose Search by IP (or use the simulator), to calculate an approximate location. Our server, by contrast, does not send it: it estimates your country with the “IP to Country Lite” database from DB-IP (db-ip.com, Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license), which it queries locally and which does not receive any of your data.

Hosting providers: DigitalOcean, where the site runs and the activity log is stored, and Hugging Face, where the service that creates the payment sessions runs, as well as the one that receives Stripe notifications and sends each purchase to Google Analytics.

OpenAI: if whoever administers the site uses its internal analysis assistant, the results of its queries on the activity log, which may include phone numbers and identifiers, are processed by that service.

sections.title: Cookies and local storage
paragraphs: We use two cookies of our own that do not depend on your consent because they are necessary: one that remembers your language for one year (only if you choose a language) and another, called cookie_consent, that remembers your cookie choice for 180 days and contains no personal identifier.

The site detects, from your IP address or from your browser’s time zone, whether you are in the European Economic Area (the European Union plus Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway), the United Kingdom or Switzerland. If so, it shows you a cookie notice and does not load Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics or Google Ads, nor store measurement data on your device, until you allow it. You can accept all, reject all or choose by category (analytics and advertising), and change your choice whenever you want using the “Cookie preferences” link at the bottom of every page. If you withdraw a permission, we delete the Google cookies for that category and, if necessary, reload the page.

Outside those regions, Google Analytics and Google Ads create their own cookies as soon as you open the page, without a prior consent notice, to measure usage and campaigns. You can block or delete them from your browser settings.

Your browser also stores data in its local storage to make the page work and to measure its use. In those regions, the measurement data (such as the numbers you used in the simulator with the location assigned to them, the campaign parameters and the status of a payment in progress) is stored only if you allow it; the position of the map you are going to pay for is always stored, for up to 24 hours, to give it back to you when you return from Stripe. You can delete this data from your browser settings.

sections.title: Data retention
paragraphs: We do not delete the activity logs automatically: we keep them for as long as they remain useful for the purposes described. We store backup copies of the database; the daily ones are replaced over time and some historical files are kept with no expiration date.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: You can ask to access, rectify or delete your data, or object to its processing, by writing to the contact listed below. To find your records we need the phone number you used in the simulator or your browser’s analytics identifier (the Google Analytics _ga cookie), because we do not store your name or your email in them. Deletion applies to the active database; backup copies are replaced over time, and historical files are only modified upon express request. If you are in the European Union, you can also file a complaint with your data protection authority.

sections.title: Changes
paragraphs: We will update this page when the processing of the data changes.
